sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) Which compound forms the ethyl carbocation? (b) Give two examples of nucleophiles.
questions.answer: (a) Bromoethane/chloroethane (C2H5X) by heterolytic fission of the C–X bond: C2H5Br → C2H5+ + Br−. (b) OH−, CN− (also NH3, H2O).

questions.q: (a) Write the IUPAC name of CH3CH2SH. (b) Arrange in decreasing order of stability: CH3+, (CH3)3C+, (CH3)2CH+.
State true or false: (a) –NO2 shows the –I effect. (b) Carbocations are planar sp² hybridised.
Fill in: (a) Cleavage in which each atom takes one electron of the bond is called ______ fission. (b) Carbocations are ______ deficient.
Match: (a) –OH (b) –CHO (c) –COOH with (i) carboxylic acid (ii) alcohol (iii) aldehyde.
Give (a) the IUPAC name of CH3CH(OH)CH3 and (b) its functional group.
State the type of isomerism in (a) butane and 2-methylpropane (b) propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol.
Name (a) an electrophile and (b) a free-radical initiator.
questions.answer: (a) NO2+ (or H+, AlCl3). (b) A peroxide, e.g. benzoyl peroxide, or UV light/heat for Cl2.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is heterolytic fission? What are the species formed?
questions.answer: Cleavage of a covalent bond in which the shared pair goes to one atom, forming a cation and an anion (carbocation or carbanion). They initiate reactions as electrophiles or nucleophiles.

questions.q: What is the –I effect? Give two groups showing it.
questions.answer: The permanent displacement of the electron cloud of a σ bond towards a more electronegative atom or group; –NO2 and –COOH (also –CN, –Cl) show –I effect.

questions.q: Why is a tertiary carbocation more stable than a primary carbocation?
questions.answer: Three alkyl groups release electrons by +I effect and provide more hyperconjugation structures (nine C–H bonds), dispersing the positive charge.

questions.q: Write the IUPAC names of CH3CH2SH and CH3CH2CHO.
What is hyperconjugation? Give one example.
questions.answer: Delocalisation of σ electrons of a C–H bond adjacent to an unsaturated centre or carbocation; the ethyl carbocation CH3CH2+ is stabilised by it.

questions.q: Distinguish between an electrophile and a nucleophile with one example each.
questions.answer: An electrophile is electron-deficient (accepts a pair), e.g. NO2+; a nucleophile is electron-rich (donates a pair), e.g. OH−.

questions.q: What are isomers? State the isomerism shown by but-2-ene.
questions.answer: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different structures; but-2-ene shows cis–trans (geometrical) isomerism.

questions.q: What is a homologous series? Give two characteristics.
questions.answer: A series of compounds with the same functional group, with successive members differing by a CH2 unit; they have a general formula and similar chemical properties with gradation in physical properties.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Write the IUPAC names of (a) CH3CH(CH3)CH2OH (b) CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3 (c) CH3CH2COOH.
Explain the stability of carbocations with the order of stability and reasons.
questions.answer: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH3+. Alkyl groups donate electrons through the +I effect and through hyperconjugation (the number of C–H hyperconjugative structures increases from 0 in CH3+ to 9 in (CH3)3C+), which disperses the positive charge.

questions.q: Explain the inductive effect and its effect on the acidity of carboxylic acids.
questions.answer: The permanent polarisation of a σ bond by an electronegative group; –I groups such as Cl stabilise the carboxylate and increase the acidity (ClCH2COOH is stronger than CH3COOH), while +I groups (alkyl) decrease it (HCOOH is stronger than CH3COOH).

questions.q: Distinguish between structural and stereo isomerism with examples of chain and optical isomers.
questions.answer: Structural isomers differ in the connectivity of atoms (butane and isobutane). Stereoisomers have the same connectivity but different arrangement in space (cis/trans-but-2-ene, d- and l-lactic acid, which has a chiral carbon).

questions.q: What are free radicals? How are they formed? Give the order of stability.
questions.answer: Neutral species with an unpaired electron formed by homolytic fission with heat, light or a peroxide (Cl2 → 2Cl•). Stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl.

questions.q: How are organic compounds purified by (a) crystallisation (b) fractional distillation?
questions.answer: (a) The impure solid is dissolved in a hot solvent and filtered; on cooling, pure crystals separate. (b) A mixture of liquids with close boiling points is heated through a fractionating column; the component of lower boiling point distils first.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) State the IUPAC rules for naming an organic compound. (b) Write the IUPAC names of CH3CH2CH(OH)CH3, CH3COOH, CH3CH2NH2, CH3CH=CHCH3 and CH3CH2SH.
questions.answer:
(a) Select the longest chain containing the principal functional group; number it to give the lowest locant to the principal group, then to multiple bonds and substituents; name substituents alphabetically; use the suffix of the principal group (-ol, -al, -one, -oic acid, -amine, -thiol, -ene).
(b) Butan-2-ol; ethanoic acid; ethanamine; but-2-ene; ethanethiol.

questions.q: (a) Explain inductive, resonance and hyperconjugation effects with examples. (b) Arrange CH3COOH, ClCH2COOH and FCH2COOH in increasing order of acidic strength and explain.
questions.answer:
(a) Inductive: permanent polarisation of σ bonds (–Cl). Resonance: delocalisation of π electrons (carboxylate ion, benzene). Hyperconjugation: C–H σ electrons delocalised into an adjacent empty p orbital (ethyl carbocation).
(b) CH3COOH < ClCH2COOH < FCH2COOH. The –I effect of F is greater than that of Cl, stabilising the anion more.

questions.q: (a) Distinguish between homolytic and heterolytic fission. (b) What are carbocations, carbanions and free radicals? Give the order of the stability of carbocations. (c) Name two electrophiles and two nucleophiles.
questions.answer:
(a) Homolytic: each atom gets one electron, giving radicals; heterolytic: the pair goes to one atom, giving ions.
(b) Carbocation: positive carbon with six electrons (sp², planar); carbanion: negative carbon with a lone pair (sp³, pyramidal); free radical: carbon with an unpaired electron. Stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > CH3+.
(c) Electrophiles: H+, NO2+; nucleophiles: OH−, CN−.

questions.q: (a) Explain different types of structural isomerism with one example each. (b) Draw the cis and trans isomers of but-2-ene and write the reason for geometrical isomerism.
questions.answer:
(a) Chain – butane and 2-methylpropane; position – propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol; functional – ethanol and methoxymethane; metamerism – diethyl ether and methyl propyl ether; tautomerism – keto and enol forms.
(b) cis-but-2-ene has both CH3 groups on the same side of the C=C; trans has them on opposite sides. Geometrical isomerism arises from restricted rotation about the C=C double bond with two different groups on each carbon.
